newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will hold a news conference at 1400 local on the budget revision and adjustments to the loan memorandum signed with the International Monetary Fund in April. The national radio will broadcast the conference live.

* The upper Senate's defence commission said labour unions from the oil refining sector in the Prahova county were planning street protests against the government's decision to scrap the Romanian Oil Company authority and to set up a new oil utility. Labour leaders fear that the move would lead to the closure of most oil refineries.

* Romania should set up a national mining agency as a government body in charge with restructuring or closing down mines, mining trade unions confederation leader Marin Condescu told a news conference. The government has no strategy for mining restructuring, Condescu said.

* Representatives of mining unions were scheduled to meet cabinet members on Thursday. Condescu said his organisation favoured mining sector reform, but threatened labour protests unless the government solves problems facing the sector.

* Floods which hit Romania in the past two weeks have killed 20 people, affecting 32 of the country's 42 counties, and submerging 300,000 hectares of various crop land, Environment Minister Ioan Oltean told a news conference.
Oltean said floods destroyed more than 24,000 homes across the country and caused damage worth some 800 billion lei, or four times his ministry's budget for 1997.

* After the budget revision, the environment ministry has been stripped of six billion lei from ititial allocations, Oltean said. He said the cuts would force the ministry to stop works to preventing further flood damage.
* Oltean said his ministry would look for alternative funding, from local and special taxes and from fines levied from industrial polluters.
